execution_steps: 1. Read Event 321's own exact_next_action, which named this exact task as the higher-leverage option over continuing per-format obligation closure, since this invariant is program-wide (blocked for all six formats simultaneously by one missing matrix entry) rather than per-format.
2. Confirmed via grep that packaging/python/package-matrix.yaml genuinely had no `format_id: ora` entry (5 of the 6 FF6 formats did: ipynb, nrrd, safetensors, ubl, xliff).

3. Verified ora's own packaging readiness directly before assuming it would work: read src/python/ora/pyproject.toml (name=format-factory-ora, requires-python>=3.11, single dependency format-factory-core==0.1.0.dev0, matching every sibling FF6 format's own shape exactly), confirmed format_factory.ora.__init__ exports a load() callable, and ran load() directly against samples/by-format/ora/valid/minimal.ora in a scratch script to confirm the exact smoke-test shape before committing it to the matrix.

4. Added the ora entry to package-matrix.yaml between nrrd and safetensors (matching the file's existing alphabetical ordering), using xliff's own entry as the direct structural template (build_mode: native_pyproject, install_proof.expected: object, smoke_callable: load, local_dependencies: format-factory-core) -- no invented fields, no deviation from the established schema.
5. Validated the YAML parses and the new entry round-trips (yaml.safe_load, confirmed 'ora' in the parsed format_id list, 27 total formats now).

6. Ran tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format ora alone first (1/1 PASS) to isolate and confirm the new matrix entry itself works correctly before attempting the more expensive full 6-format run.

7. Ran tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format nrrd --format ora --format xliff --format ipynb --format safetensors --format ubl -- the first time this mission has ever attempted a genuine all-six-format co-install. RESULT: 6/6 PASS. Inspected the resulting proof-manifest.json directly per-format: nrrd/ora/xliff/ipynb/safetensors all 0 failed deep imports; ubl had the same 2 pre-existing failures (setuptools, ff_csv) already documented in every prior compatibility-gate.json this session -- confirmed these are NOT new, NOT collisions, and NOT caused by ora's own presence.

8. Wrote reports/certification/ff6-six-format-co-install-gate.json as a new, program-wide (not per-format) evidence record -- placed at the top level of reports/certification/ alongside the existing cross-product-parity.json, since no per-format directory is the right home for a program-wide invariant.

9. Updated the 3 existing per-format compatibility-gate.json files (ipynb, safetensors, xliff) that had each previously documented and explicitly flagged the 5-format-only proof with ora excluded -- corrected each to cite the new 6/6 result and cross-reference the new program-wide gate file, rather than leaving 3 now-stale 'ora excluded' notes standing uncorrected.

10. Ran the full ora test suite (349 passed, unchanged) to confirm the matrix addition itself caused zero regression to ora's own product code (it did not touch any src/ file, only a packaging manifest entry).
